# Markov Chains and Steady-State Distributions

Markov chains underlie MDPs in RL, HMMs in NLP/speech, PageRank, and MCMC sampling.

## The Markov Property

P(X_{t+1}=j | X_t=i, X_{t-1},…) = P(X_{t+1}=j | X_t=i)

**Transition matrix P**: Pᵢⱼ = P(X_{t+1}=j|X_t=i). Rows sum to 1 (stochastic). n-step transitions: P^n (matrix power).

## Stationary Distribution

π satisfies: **πᵀP = πᵀ**, Σᵢπᵢ=1

Left eigenvector of P for eigenvalue 1. Compute via power iteration or solving (P−I)ᵀπ=0.

## Ergodicity

- **Irreducible**: every state reachable from every other
- **Aperiodic**: gcd{n: Pⁿᵢᵢ>0}=1 (no periodic cycling)

**Ergodic theorem**: irreducible + aperiodic → P^n→𝟙πᵀ and (1/T)Σf(X_t)→E_π[f] a.s.

Foundation of MCMC: time averages → posterior expectations.

## Detailed Balance (Reversibility)

πᵢPᵢⱼ = πⱼPⱼᵢ → π is stationary. MH and Gibbs both satisfy detailed balance by construction.

## Mixing Time and Spectral Gap

τ_mix ~ 1/Δ where **Δ = 1 − |λ₂|** is the spectral gap (λ₂ = second eigenvalue of P).

Large Δ → fast mixing. Small Δ (λ₂ close to 1) → slow mixing (bottleneck in graph).

```python
P = np.array([[0.7,0.2,0.1],[0.3,0.4,0.3],[0.2,0.3,0.5]])
# Stationary distribution
eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eig(P.T)
pi = eigenvectors[:, np.argmax(eigenvalues.real)].real
pi /= pi.sum()
# Spectral gap
gap = 1 - sorted(abs(np.linalg.eigvals(P)), reverse=True)[1]
print(f"Spectral gap: {gap:.4f}, mixing time ~ {1/gap:.1f}")
```

## PageRank as Markov Chain

P(next=j|cur=i) = (1−d)/|S| + d·A_{ij}/out(i), d=0.85

Damping makes chain irreducible and aperiodic → unique stationary distribution = PageRank vector.

Power iteration converges at rate d^t ≈ 0.85^t — ~50-100 iterations for web-scale.

## Markov Chains in RL

MDP under fixed policy π: P_π(s'|s) = Σₐ π(a|s) P(s'|s,a) — a Markov chain.

Bellman equation: V^π(s) = Σₐ π(a|s) Σ_{s'} P(s'|s,a) [R + γV^π(s')] — linear system.

Ergodicity ensures policy gradient theorem holds: gradient of average reward = stationary expectation.

## Hidden Markov Models

Latent Markov chain z_t + emission p(x_t|z_t).

- **Forward algorithm**: P(z_t|x_{1:t}) — O(TK²)
- **Forward-backward**: P(z_t|x_{1:T}) — smoothing
- **Viterbi**: argmax P(z_{1:T}|x_{1:T}) — O(TK²)
- **Baum-Welch**: EM for parameter learning

Used in speech recognition, gene finding, sequence models.
